Stop maintaining your own Puppeteer setup. There is a simpler way.


If you have a Puppeteer instance running in production, you know the maintenance tax.
Chromium updates break things on a schedule you do not control. Memory leaks accumulate until you are restarting the process on a cron job. It started with a Puppeteer instance I was tired of babysitting.

I kept choosing option three, which felt wrong.

The screenshot API came first. Then someone asked about PDFs. Then I needed OG images for…

articles.author: Ned C
articles.description:
You write a .mdc rule. It looks fine. Cursor ignores it completely.
The problem is usually something small: a missing alwaysApply field, malformed YAML frontmatter, a glob pattern that doesn't match anything. You don't find out until you're mid-session and the AI does whatever it wants.
I built cursor-lint to catch this stuff before it wastes your time. Here's how to run it locally and in CI.
cursor-lint checks for the things that silently break rules:
Missing or malformed YAML frontmatter in .mdc files
alwaysApply not set (agent mode won't load the rule)
Empty rule bodies (file exists but does nothing)
Invalid glob patterns in the globs field
.cursorrules files with issues that Cursor won't report
These aren't hypothetical. I tested each failure mode: malformed YAML and missing frontmatte…
articles.title: How to Lint Your Cursor Rules in CI (So Broken Rules Don't Ship)
